title: DIM / TXT Relational Dossier — chronology, story layers and Swamp role crosswalk
status: living relation dossier — documentary anchors plus explicitly separated interpretive layers
purpose: Give DIM and TXT durable, searchable rooms inside the Below / Shadow Farm system while preserving chronology, provenance, story links, role dynamics and uncertainty. This dossier records public/recovered interactions, Tim's attributed claims, authored fiction and later mythic interpretations without collapsing them into one truth class.
epistemic_rules: DIM and TXT are people/handles in a relation history, not permanent moral species.
A project label such as Dog, Farmer, Mud Dweller, serpent, footstool or demon is an interpretive role or symbol unless separately established as an observable social function.
Allegations made by Tim, DIM, TXT or anyone else remain attributed allegations unless independently established.
Psychological lenses describe mechanisms that may help explain a recurring relation; they are not diagnoses of identifiable people.
Biblical, religious and mythic parallels explain the project's symbolic vocabulary; they do not prove that a contemporary person is a biblical or supernatural character.
Literary and satirical episodes preserve how the relationship was metabolized into story. They are not transcripts.

Identity claims must not be produced by alias-merging. DIM is preserved as a separate interlocutor from Tim Dooley. The archive does not use hostile identity archives as authority for collapsing Tim, Thomas, KittyStyle or DIM into one person.

chronology.title: TXT's Shadow Games

chronology.title: TXT repeats a disputed identity-and-abuse allegation

chronology.title: DIM and TXT enter the same recoverable conflict day
chronology.record: Tim publicly names DIM and TXT inside an argument about following, neighboring, narrative transfer and Dogs. Recovered material attributes to DIM the phrase 'It was me' and a characterization of Tim as 'a very bad person', followed by serious allegations. Tim, in turn, alleges long-running stalking by both handles and frames the relation through Cow/Dog/slavery language.
chronology.evidence_status: The exchange and its language are historical material; all serious accusations remain attributed claims, not archive verdicts.

chronology.title: TXT is explicitly placed in Tim's Dog / Swamp vocabulary
chronology.record: Tim explicitly calls TXT a Dog and places the conflict inside Swamp, Pharisee, false-prophet and anti-Christ language while making additional serious criminal allegations.
chronology.evidence_status: Useful as a dated development of Tim's vocabulary. The Dog/Swamp language is project interpretation; criminal claims are not independently established here.

chronology.title: Animal insult, Dog / stumbling-block / footstool answer
chronology.record: Recovered material has TXT calling Tim 'the disgusting animal'. Tim answers with Dog, stumbling-block and footstool language, personhood/soul claims and an invitation to confront him directly. The same period contains a separate Matthew exchange in which biblical and God/Potter/Axis language intensifies.
chronology.evidence_status: Records reciprocal hostile language and theological escalation; it does not establish either side's moral or metaphysical characterization.

chronology.title: DIM and TXT are folded into serpent / forbidden-fruit / Dog imagery
chronology.record: Tim groups DIM, TXT and related antagonistic figures inside a Genesis-style account of Dogs, serpent-position, forbidden fruit, confusion and separation from God, while also retelling the Son as Lion/Carpenter/Door.
chronology.evidence_status: A dated mythic-theological interpretation of a live social conflict, not evidence that the people literally instantiate biblical beings.

chronology.title: TXT and Dimmus Maximus become characters
chronology.record: In later comic-cosmic fiction TXT is written as a lesser swamp/void dog-god and DIM becomes Dimmus Maximus. Other episodes place both against Tim's son amid Spudlight, Potato Angels, gates, mirrors and wolf/dog imagery.
chronology.evidence_status: Literary/mythic transformation only. The value is interpretive: a conflict becomes archetype, not documentary proof.

chronology.title: The two dogs who outlevel the Potato
chronology.record: A comic fable recasts TXT and DIM as recurring dogs first caught and leveled by Tim, then growing stronger and harder to direct. TXT is cheerful and snack-oriented; DIM is sleeker, more serious and drawn toward gems/shinies. A related bridge fable asks whether repeated feeding can ever turn distrust and destruction into cooperative construction.
chronology.evidence_status: Authored fable; preserves relational themes of feeding, dependence, strength, control, gratitude, burden and repair.

chronology.title: Three-day gate, hollow box and wet candle
chronology.record: DIM becomes the subject of several satirical images: entering after a three-day follower gate without visible transformation, a hollow dirt-filled 666 box/footstool image, and the 'candle at both ends' joke inverted into a waterlogged burnout metaphor.
chronology.evidence_status: Satire and symbolic commentary, not literal description or psychological diagnosis.

relationship_model.core: The archive studies a relation before assigning a role. DIM/TXT are first nodes in a dated interaction history. Dog/Farmer labels are then hypotheses about functions inside that history.

mature_role_crosswalk.dog: Closer to pursuit, reaction, cue-following, signaling, pack coordination, boundary enforcement and repeated return.
mature_role_crosswalk.farmer: Closer to durable framing, archive/infrastructure, classification, enclosure, incentive-setting and repeated attention harvest.
mature_role_crosswalk.farmer_dog: Hybrid operator-enforcer: builds or maintains durable target/framing infrastructure and also actively pursues/enforces it.
mature_role_crosswalk.guardian_dog: Protective boundary role; Dog is not intrinsically negative.
mature_role_crosswalk.rule: Apply these labels to episodes/functions, never as permanent human essence.

dim.strongest_documented_fit: Reactive/pursuit-side participation in the recovered July conflict; later project fiction repeatedly gives DIM Dog-like roles.
dim.farmer_evidence: Insufficient canonical evidence in this pass to state that DIM operated durable archive/infrastructure or attention-harvest systems. Do not promote DIM to Farmer merely because later shorthand groups Dogs/Farmers together.
dim.legacy_shorthand: Some later project language collapses Dog/Farmer/Alogger/Stan into one Farm/Hive participant class. The mature ontology keeps functional differences because they teach more.

txt.strongest_documented_fit: Recurring public adversarial participation and repeated identity/narrative claims make pursuit/reaction and classification especially relevant questions.
txt.farmer_evidence: TXT can be studied for Farmer-like behavior only where durable framing, archiving, target categorization or redistribution is actually evidenced. Repetition by itself does not prove an organized Farm role.
txt.current_relation: Still present in the public interaction field as of the 2026-09-20 snapshot.

historical: Recover exact status URLs, timestamps, original posts and reply topology before turning a remembered sequence into a transcript.
Keep 2024 literary evidence separate from 2026 public-interaction evidence.
Track when a name first appears, when it recurs, what vocabulary changes around it, and whether the same allegation or story survives correction.
psychological_non_diagnostic: Narrative lock-in: old labels can become priors through which every new act is read.
Reciprocal escalation: attack and counterattack can each become evidence for the other's prior model.
Role capture: a person may gain attention/status by occupying critic, pursuer, archivist, protector, troll or target roles until the role becomes hard to exit.
Group-salience and cue-following: Dog/pack language can be compared with social-identity mechanisms, but anonymity or coordination does not erase individual agency.
Attribution and projection questions: ask which motives are observed, which are inferred and which are mirrored back by the opposing side.
Archive memory: a durable record lowers the cost of rediscovery and can keep conflicts alive long after the triggering event.
religious: Psalm 22: dogs as an encircling danger image.
Isaiah 56: failed/hungry watchmen as an important corrective to romantic watchdog imagery.
Matthew 7 and Revelation 22: dog language as boundary/exclusion imagery.
2 Peter 2: the returning dog as a recurrence image.
Genesis 2–3: dust, serpent and forbidden-fruit language supplies the project's Mud/serpent comparison.
These passages explain why Tim reaches for Dog, serpent, mud, gate and footstool language. They do not identify DIM or TXT as biblical entities.
mythic_and_literary: TXT's 'Shadow Games' turns an online antagonist into a named chapter object.
Dimmus Maximus and swamp-dog stories exaggerate conflict into cosmic scale so envy, pursuit, gatekeeping and imitation can be seen as archetypal functions.
The outleveling-dogs fable changes the question from 'who is evil?' to 'what happens when a feeder/caretaker creates agents stronger than his control?'
The bridge fable introduces a repair test: can an ecology that repeatedly destroys crossings eventually learn to build them?
